findings.correction: Caller namespace depth mapping; signaling moved to an opened process directory descriptor bound to the reviewed child.
findings.problem: Taking child NSpid[-1] may use a different PID namespace from the signaling caller.

findings.correction: Opened /proc/PID descriptor, descriptor-relative stat and immediate PPID validation, pidfd_send_signal; no numeric PID signal in coordinator cleanup.
findings.problem: Numeric kill after checking stat/starttime can target a reused PID; check and use are not bound.

findings.correction: Small R3S-only all-TID union with PPID-scan fallback; fixed inherited helper is unchanged. Claim remains scoped to the fixed jobs and sampled process information.
findings.problem: Frozen monitor main-TID children interface alone can miss live children forked by another thread.

findings.evidence: Static call flow arm_deadline -> execute_jobs catch -> main final identity/full file_hashes, or final identity catch -> full file_hashes. Existing 45 tests do not exercise this expiry path.
findings.problem: A one-shot campaign SIGALRM is caught by execute_jobs or final identity handling, then nonessential final source/input/runtime or full output hashing can continue without an armed wall deadline.
findings.requested_minimum_correction: Preserve an absolute hard deadline and durable expiry flag; skip expensive closeout after expiry; bound cleanup and final receipt by remaining reserve.

scope_limits: No generic hostile-process security container claim.
No NCP compatibility, physical convergence, production readiness or measured new scientific speedup is established by this review.
